faq.help: Still have questions? Our team is ready to help.

q1.question: What is Asset Monitoring?
q1.answer: Asset monitoring refers to the use of technology to continuously track and manage assets in real-time to ensure their proper functioning and timely maintenance.

q2.question: How does the monitoring system work?
q2.answer: The monitoring system uses sensors and data collection tools to gather information about asset conditions. This data is then transmitted to a central system where it is analyzed and used to trigger alerts or maintenance actions.

q3.question: What are the benefits of asset monitoring?
q3.answer: Asset monitoring provides real-time insights into asset performance, helps in early detection of potential issues, reduces maintenance costs, and enhances the overall efficiency and lifespan of assets.

q4.question: Can the system be customized for specific needs?
q4.answer: Yes, our asset monitoring solutions can be customized to meet specific requirements and adapt to various types of assets and industries. We work with you to tailor the system according to your needs.

q5.question: What kind of support is available?
q5.answer: We offer comprehensive support including technical assistance, training, and maintenance services to ensure that your monitoring system operates smoothly and effectively.

eews.title: Earthquake Warning System (EEWS)
eews.body: By identifying P-waves, the first waves to arrive in an earthquake, our system provides crucial alerts seconds to minutes before the stronger S-waves hit. This early notification allows users to take swift actions, such as moving to a safer location or halting critical operations, ultimately saving lives and minimizing damage.

buildings.title: BUILDINGS
buildings.copy: Earthquakes can cause severe damage, including the collapse of buildings, often on a large scale, and can result in casualties. These sudden events trigger widespread panic and chaos. Building damage may also disrupt electricity supply, cause gas pipe leaks, and even lead to explosions. Public services are disrupted, endangering critical surgical procedures and valuable equipment in hospitals, as well as putting the safety of children in schools at risk. The AMTI Earthquake Early Warning System (EEWS) can reduce the risk of damage and casualties by integrating with Building Management Systems. This EEWS can mitigate earthquake impacts by initiating preventive actions such as activating safe mode for equipment, elevators, and gates, reducing gas pressure, shutting off wastewater lines, cutting power, and issuing warnings via social media, SMS, WhatsApp, alarms, and audiovisual systems. Additionally, the system can automatically halt sensitive procedures to minimize further damage.

transportation.title: TRANSPORTATION
transportation.copy: Earthquakes pose a serious threat to transportation systems such as airports, ports, railways, and vehicles, potentially disrupting operations and endangering passengers and operators. By providing early warnings, authorities can quickly implement safety protocols, protecting lives and critical infrastructure. The Earthquake Early Warning System (EEWS) from AMTI can intervene by activating automatic emergency braking mechanisms for trains, redirecting air traffic and triggering warnings on road signs to prevent accidents and ensure the safety of passengers and workers.

utilities.title: UTILITIES
utilities.copy: Earthquake vibrations can damage pipelines, valves, and pump stations, causing hazardous chemical and water leaks that could disrupt vital supplies of clean water or electricity to the community. The Earthquake Early Warning System (EEWS) from AMTI can trigger preventive actions to protect power plants, such as reducing gas pressure, preventing hydrogen evaporation, safeguarding substations, cutting off wastewater flow, and halting the supply of electricity and water. Additionally, the system can generate post-event reports to assess potential damage to pipelines.
actions: Control water pressure in fire mains

oilGasChemicals.title: OIL, GAS AND CHEMICALS
oilGasChemicals.copy: Earthquakes can cause explosions, fires, chemical leaks, and environmental damage at oil and gas facilities. With AMTI's earthquake early warning, there is more time to trigger damage control actions, such as lowering or shutting off gas pressure, with maximum response time. This limits potential damage while keeping critical infrastructure and vital services operational. EEWS AMTI also sends alerts via social media, SMS, WhatsApp, alarms, or audiovisual systems to employees, reducing injuries and casualties, and speeding up facility recovery.
actions: Control water pressure in fire mains

mines.title: MINES
mines.copy: Earthquakes can cause significant damage to infrastructure and jeopardize worker safety in mining operations. The Earthquake Early Warning System (EEWS) from AMTI can significantly reduce damage, primarily by warning workers and giving them time to take cover or evacuate before the main tremor hits. Earthquake alerts can also trigger automatic shutdown mechanisms for critical mining equipment and isolate hazardous materials, reducing the risk of damage to machinery and ensuring team safety. Post-event reports can support decision-making processes for resuming operations after an earthquake.

shms.label: SHMS
shms.title: Structure Health Monitoring System (SHMS)
shms.body: A structure health monitoring (SHM) system is a system that continuously monitors structures like buildings and bridges to assess their integrity and detect damage.

bridges.title: BRIDGES
bridges.copy: Our SHMS is designed to monitor the health of bridges in real time, providing critical insights into structural integrity and potential wear. Timely alerts enable preventive maintenance and ensure long-term safety, helping prevent catastrophic failures and prolonging infrastructure lifespan.

buildings.title: BUILDINGS
buildings.copy: Our SHMS monitors critical infrastructures, from skyscrapers to hospitals, offering real-time data on structural health. This enables maintenance teams to make informed decisions to prevent costly repairs and improve safety for occupants.

dam.title: DAM
dam.copy: Continuous structural health monitoring for dams provides real-time detection of seepage, deformation, and hydrostatic pressure changes. By tracking concrete integrity and seismic responses, our system empowers operators to prevent catastrophic failures, safeguard downstream communities, and maintain water resource security.

landslide.title: LANDSLIDE
landslide.copy: Our geotechnical and slope health monitoring system delivers early detection of ground displacement, soil saturation, and slope instability. Continuous real-time sensor analytics provide timely warnings before critical movement occurs, protecting transportation corridors, vital infrastructure, and nearby communities from landslide hazards.

port.title: PORT
port.copy: Designed for harsh marine environments, our SHMS tracks the integrity of quay walls, piers, and heavy cargo berths under dynamic tidal loads and berthing forces. Real-time telemetry detects structural settlement and fatigue early, ensuring uninterrupted harbor logistics and extended terminal longevity.

railway.title: RAILWAY
railway.copy: Rail infrastructure monitoring offers continuous assessment of tracks, viaducts, and overhead structures under repetitive high-speed train loads. Instant alerts on vibration anomalies, track alignment shifts, and foundation stress help maintenance crews prevent derailment risks and optimize maintenance schedules without service disruption.

tunnels.title: TUNNELS
tunnels.copy: With SHMS, tunnel safety is greatly enhanced through real-time monitoring of structural stress and vibration. This system allows for immediate responses to potential threats, safeguarding both infrastructure and people.
